# Code review: pending invitees lose access to space data (`ff7c782…HEAD`)

**Mode:** committed range, as you asked. 12 files, +341 −79 · base `ff7c782` → `HEAD` `4f4aaba` (2 commits).
**Repo:** safe-client-gateway · TypeScript/NestJS · Jest · 4 stated rules in AGENTS.md (layering, updating specs when dependencies change, pre-commit gates, SPDX headers) · 9 of 9 areas have code to review.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fine to open the PR. One test issue is worth fixing first. |
| **Score** | **~94 / 100** (1 of 5 findings verified by two agents; the other 4 count at full weight) |
| **Held the score down** | Testing: an unchanged end-to-end test still asserts the old behaviour for invited members |
| **Fix first** | F1 |

The change itself looks correct. Only two places still use the "active or pending member" rule: `findSpaces` and `findActiveOrInvitedMemberOrFail`. Both now cut a pending invitee's view down to their own row. `assertMember`, `findAllowed` and `updateAlias` now require an ACTIVE member. `invitedByName` still resolves correctly for the invitee's own row, because `memberUserIds` is still built from the full list of members.

## Fix before opening

**F1 · P2 · Testing · CONFIRMED (validator confirmed, refuter could not defeat it)**
`src/modules/spaces/routes/spaces.controller.e2e-spec.ts:511` and `src/modules/spaces/routes/address-books.controller.e2e-spec.ts:799`
- **What:** The test "Should return a space by its id for an invited member" is unchanged. It still expects an invitee to see the admin's ACTIVE row, which is exactly what this change removes. Its member token is `jwtService.sign(siweAuthPayloadDtoBuilder().build())`, whose `sub` is a random single digit and not the invitee's real user id.
- **Why it matters:** Auth resolves the user only from `sub` (`src/modules/auth/utils/assert-authenticated.utils.ts:30`). So this test never really acts as the invitee, and GET `/spaces/:id` has no end-to-end test for the new trimmed view. The `createPendingMember` helper in `address-books.controller.e2e-spec.ts`, renamed in this diff, has the same problem. Its "declined membership → 404" test (L183) can't tell a declined invitee from a stranger.
- **Correction from the validator:** the unbound token was there before this diff. The request most likely 404s at `spaces.service.ts:69-73` before it reaches the new filter. So the test is flaky or passes by coincidence, rather than failing reliably now.
- **Fix:** Sign the invitee token with `accessTokenForUserId(inviteResponse.body[0].userId)`. That is the pattern already used, with an explanatory comment, at `members.controller.e2e-spec.ts:71-76` and in `user-address-book.controller.e2e-spec.ts`. Then assert that `members` has length 1 (the invitee only) and `safeCount` is 0.

Invitees now get their own row only and `safeCount: 0`. Only `members.controller.ts:240` was updated. | Add the same note used on the members endpoint |

| F5 | `src/modules/users/domain/members.repository.ts:513` | The optional `relations` parameter is now always passed `{ user: true }` by both callers. The JSDoc explaining why it varied was deleted in this diff. | Hard-code `relations: { user: true }` and drop the parameter |

## Worth tidying (no score impact)
One proposal, about 60 lines: `createActiveMember` is now written out three times with the same body:
- `address-book-requests.controller.e2e-spec.ts:522`
- `address-books.controller.e2e-spec.ts:818`

Keeping helpers per spec file is how the repo already works, so this is optional. The tidy-up is to move it into a shared e2e helper next to `accessTokenForUserId`.

Reply **fix**, **ticket** or **skip** for that proposal. No answer counts as skip.
